subject: Northbridge: Air-gapped private K8s deployment — preflight & node/storage plan
messages:
From: Claire Wong <claire.wong@northbridge-med.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridge-med.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment — air-gapped requirements & inventory attached

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this. We're moving forward with a private (on-prem, VPC-isolated) deployment of Redwood for a pilot at Northbridge Medical. Before the procurement paperwork, the security and infra teams need a concrete preflight checklist and a proposed node/storage topology that meets our constraints. High-level constraints: 

- No outbound internet from cluster (air-gapped).
- Image registry hosted internally; we need guidance on offline registry sync and remote signing verification.
- FIPS 140-2 compliant crypto required (HSM preferred for key material).
- PV encryption at rest; long-term retention for logs (90d) with archiving to internal NFS.
- Kubernetes will be managed by our infra team, target k8s version 1.25 initially (we can upgrade).
- No GPUs for pilot; CPU nodes only, but need plan if/when GPU is introduced.
- Expected qps: 40 concurrent inference sessions, burst to 120. Token footprint small but steady.

I've attached an inventory spreadsheet and a network diagram (northbridge-inventory.xlsx, northbridge-network-diagram.pdf). Can you: 1) send a concise preflight checklist we can map to procurement, 2) recommend node pool sizes and PV class mapping, 3) confirm any KMS/HSM integration constraints and doc links we can share with Security?

Looking for a short workshop next week (60m) with engineering and security to walk through the gaps.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Wong
IT Infrastructure Lead | Northbridge Medical
attachments: northbridge-inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet), northbridge-network-diagram.pdf (pdf)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@northbridge-med.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridge-med.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-18T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — air-gapped requirements & inventory attached

Hi Claire — thanks for the inventory and diagram. Looping in Rishi (inference infra), Laura (deployment ops), and Irene (security) so we can give a consolidated preflight and map responsibilities.

High level next steps from our side (proposed):
1) 60m preflight workshop (we'll prep an outline) — propose Feb 24 or Feb 25, 10:00-11:00 PT.
2) Mapping of Northbridge inventory to our nodepool templates + PV class recommendations.
3) KMS/HSM integration options: (a) customer-managed HSM with Redwood using wrapped DEKs, (b) Redwood-managed envelope encryption with customer KMS over private link (if permitted).
4) Airgap checklist: offline image sync procedure, signing verification, initial bootstrap bundle, OS package policies, and service account provisioning.
5) Draft mutual action plan (MAP) for procurement and SOW sign-off.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Air-gapped/offline registry: we support an offline sync tool and can provide signed image bundles. We'll need a small jumpbox with outbound-only capability during sync windows (or you can provide USB-signed bundles).
- FIPS/HSM: we can integrate with customer HSMs that expose PKCS#11. We'll prepare a short HSM integration guide.
- PV encryption: recommend CSI driver that supports KMIP/KMS. We'll map log retention to a dedicated archive PV class (NFS) and recommend object-archive process off-cluster.
- K8s version: 1.25 is OK for pilot. We'll note compatibility with our runtime and recommend 1.26+ for future upgrades.

I'll attach our private preflight outline and a short checklist for procurement. Please confirm which workshop date/time works and whether your security team will join.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-private-preflight-outline.pdf (pdf)

From: Claire Wong <claire.wong@northbridge-med.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridge-med.com>
Date: 2026-02-19T08:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — air-gapped requirements & inventory attached

Hi Stephanie — Feb 24 10:00 PT works for us; I'll invite our security lead (Samir) and the infra engineer who will run the cluster. A few clarifications ahead of the call so we can be efficient: 

- We prefer a USB-signed bundle option for initial bootstrap; our environment forbids any machine with outbound connectivity unless strictly controlled. Please include the exact bundle format and verification steps.
- Our HSM vendor is Thales Luna; they expose PKCS#11 endpoints. We need a clear list of required capabilities and whether any latency-sensitive ops would call the HSM directly during inference.
- PV types: we use an internal Ceph cluster (RBD + RGW) for block/object. For logs we prefer a write-through NFS to our archive cluster. Any guidance on RWX vs RWO for Redis-like caches and LMDB/KV caches?
- Compliance: we need a short description of audit logging we can include in the SOW — specifically token retention, masking, and ways to purge for subject requests.

I've attached the network diagram and inventory you already received, plus a short internal checklist for our security gate (northbridge-network-diagram.pdf, northbridge-inventory.xlsx).

Thanks — see you on Feb 24.
Claire

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Claire Wong <claire.wong@northbridge-med.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridge-med.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — air-gapped requirements & inventory attached

Quick technical notes our infra team will bring to the workshop — saving time for Feb 24: 

1) Node pool proposal (pilot, no GPUs):
   - control-plane: 3 x m5.large equivalent (HA controllers) on isolated management VLAN; static IPs; kubeadm-managed
   - inference-pool-standard: 4 x c6i.4xlarge equivalent (8 vCPU, 32GB) with 2 x NVMe per host for local KV cache; use local ephemeral for KV cache and Ceph RBD for model artifacts and checkpoints
   - burst-pool (scale-as-needed): 2 x larger machines to handle spikes (auto-scale via on-prem autoscaler)

2) Storage mapping:
   - Models/artifacts: Ceph RBD (RWO), encrypted at rest via CSI with KMIP/KMS plug-in. Recommend separate PV class with replication factor aligned to Ceph policy.
   - KV cache and shardable caches: local NVMe (ephemeral) with a sync-to-backend snapshot job to Ceph every 6 hours.
   - Logs and audit: write-through to NFS (RWX) with lifecycle job to copy to long-term archive (offline object store). Ensure retention policy is parameterized per customer requirement.

3) HSM usage patterns:
   - Use HSM for master key wrapping and signing of image bundles. Runtime token decryption should use wrapped DEKs to avoid direct HSM calls on every inference (to keep latency low).
   - Provide a test harness for PKCS#11 with sample flows (wrap/unwrap, sign/verify).

4) Airgap & bootstrap:
   - We'll provide a signed image bundle format (OCI tar + SHA256 + signature). Verification steps: sha256sum, signature verify with provided public key, then load into your internal registry.
   - Offline sync option: bootstrap jumpbox with temporary egress for bundle sync OR physically transfer signed bundles. We'll document both.

5) Audit & data subject requests:
   - Token retention: configurable per deployment; default 30d for pilot, can extend. Masking: we support deterministic masking hooks before logs leave the runtime. Purge: periodic job plus on-demand purge API for customer data subject requests; will document APIs included in SOW.

Open questions for workshop: expected model size (GB) per artifact, batch vs streaming latency targets (p95), and whether you want local model caching across nodes or a warm pool.

I'll bring a short slide with the node/storage mapping and bootstrap examples.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
